framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: A provider that concludes an Annex III system is not high-risk (e.g. narrow procedural task) must document that assessment before placing it on the market, register it under Art. 49(2) and give it to authorities on request; profiling systems always stay high-risk.
what_is_tested: The provider's own classification assessment (documented self-assessment)
who_tests: Provider (self-assessment); national competent authorities may request

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: Commission must issue standardisation requests covering all Section 2 requirements and request deliverables facilitating joint compliance with Chapter III Sections 2-3 and Annex I product legislation.
what_is_tested: Standardisation request (a duty on the Commission)
who_tests: European Commission (requesting); European standardisation organisations (CEN, CENELEC, ETSI)

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: Providers must notify the Commission within two weeks of meeting (or learning they will meet) the systemic-risk criterion, and may argue exceptionally that their model does not present systemic risks.

framework: EU AI Act - Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-Generated Content (Section 1, providers)
requirement_paraphrase: Signatories measure detection accuracy (e.g. error rates) on varied samples, including other systems' content and data not used in training, across content length, size, diversity and semantics; they also test robustness to common processing operations (compression, cropping, paraphrasing, translation, print-and-scan) and to adversarial attacks (copying, removal, regeneration, modification of marks) using the same metrics; compliance is demonstrated before market placement and over the lifecycle.
what_is_tested: Reliability and robustness metrics for watermark/marking detection

framework: EU AI Act - GPAI Code of Practice (Safety and Security chapter)
requirement_paraphrase: To support post-market monitoring, signatories give an adequate number of independent external evaluators free access to the most capable model version on the market, its chains-of-thought if available, and the least-mitigated corresponding version (unless the model is similarly safe or safer), publish selection criteria, do not train on evaluators' test inputs/outputs without permission, and take no legal or technical retaliation against evaluators who test and publish findings within stated limits.
what_is_tested: Third-party post-market evaluation access and safe harbour

framework: Japan AISI - Guide to Evaluation Perspectives on AI Safety v1.10 (28 Mar 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: Defines ten evaluation perspectives: toxic output control; misinformation and manipulation; fairness and inclusion; high-risk/unintended use; privacy; security; explainability; robustness; data quality; verifiability.
what_is_tested: Ten safety perspectives for LLM systems
who_tests: Development and provision managers; experts inside or outside the organisation; third-party evaluation can complement (Sec. 4.1)

framework: NCA 'Draft of AI Cybersecurity Guidelines' (AICG-1:2026), draft for public consultation (closed 5 Aug 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Continuously assess the cybersecurity capabilities and resilience of AI agents throughout the development lifecycle.
what_is_tested: Cybersecurity capabilities and resilience of AI agents

framework: DoH Abu Dhabi Responsible AI Standard V1 (Oct 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: AI systems rated high risk must undergo conformity assessments both before and after deployment, coordinated with DoH's Data and Digital Governance Office.
what_is_tested: Conformity with ethical standards and statutory requirements

framework: DIFC Data Protection Regulations, proposed amendments (Annex A 'Proposed Changes' to DIFCA Consultation Paper No. 3, June 2026; draft cover 'Consolidated Version No. 3, in force on [XX 2026]'; NOT enacted as seen on 2026-10-16)
clause_or_page: Proposed Reg. 10.3.2(b), Annex A printed p.13 (current 10.3.2(b) would become 10.3.2(c))
requirement_paraphrase: Proposed: no one may use, operate or offer for commercial use a System that processes personal data unless the System has been tested for safety verification, including native regulatory and security design (in addition to human-defined purposes and design compliance with Reg. 10.3.1 and Commissioner audit, governance or certification requirements).
what_is_tested: Safety of the System, including regulatory and security design

framework: UAE AI Adoption Guideline in Government Services
clause_or_page: Execution stage, approx. pp.78-79 (locator approximate, tool-reported)
requirement_paraphrase: Once the model is ready, it is evaluated against acceptance criteria to confirm readiness for deployment.
what_is_tested: AI/ML model readiness against acceptance criteria before deployment
who_tests: Implementing government entity (not specified in text read)

framework: US NIST AI RMF 1.0 (NIST AI 100-1, January 2023)
requirement_paraphrase: The Framework is intended to be voluntary, rights-preserving, non-sector-specific and use-case agnostic.

framework: US NIST AI 800-2 ipd (CAISI) Practices for Automated Benchmark Evaluations of Language Models (Initial Public Draft, January 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Report qualified claims: distinguish observations, inferences, predictions and normative statements and tie claims to the evaluated benchmark and measurement conditions.
what_is_tested: Calibration of claims from test results
